transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-17 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM); Jordan Blake (Pelican Head of ML), Anita Shah (Platform Eng), Samir Patel (CTO), Ellen Cho (SRE)

Summary:
Quick health check and QBR-style review focused on usage trends, cost anomalies for February, reliability incidents (two brief spikes), and pilot next-steps for a dedicated capacity POC. Main ask from Pelican: keep 99th pct latency < 180ms for interactive assistants and show cost delta for ded & hosted for their bursty ecomm traffic.

Topics:
- Feb usage and cost drivers
- Reliability incidents and root cause (KV cache flushes & autoscaler config)
- Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs (burst capacity, pricing, data isolation)
- Security/compliance checklist (SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs)
- Pilot scope & timeline
- Next steps and artifacts to share

Action items (recorded in call): see metadata action_items above.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy to kick off. We're gonna run 45ish minutes, then open for Qs. Is that still good?
[00:08] Jordan Blake: Yep that works for us. Thanks Maya.
[00:12] Luis Ortega: Quick intro from the redwood side — I'm Luis, SE, I'll lead the bench plan, and Priya is our CSM for ops.
[00:20] Priya Nair: Hi team.
[00:22] Samir Patel: Good afternoon. We want to go over cost spikes in feb as well as the outage on March 2nd.
[00:30] Maya Chen: Yes, perfect. Anita, could you start with a run through of what you're seeing in the platform?
[00:35] Anita Shah: Sure. So feb was, um, higher than forecasted. We saw about a 38% jump in tokens processed week-over-week, most concentrated in the 11–14 UTC window. There were two short incidents — one around the 2nd where a config change caused aggressive KV cache invalidation, so the runtime did a lot of cold starts. It was short, about 12 minutes, but the 95/99 latencies spiked.
[01:06] Ellen Cho: yeah that one hit our checkout flow, which is time-sensitive. It looked like an autoscaler misfire, the policy bounced nodes a little too aggressively.
[01:15] Luis Ortega: Right, from our side we saw the batch sizing fall to 1 for several minutes which kills throughput and increases per-token cost. Also noticed quantization path fell back to fp16 on some GPUs — I think that was the model variant mismatch.
[01:32] Jordan Blake: A quick clarification — when you say prefix KV cache invalidation, do you mean the prefix cache or the kv cache? I saw K V cash in the logs, little weird.
[01:40] Luis Ortega: Sorry, yeah, prefix/KV cache. Might be a transcription issue in the logs, the system registered a manual cache flush that then triggered many cold loads.
[01:48] Samir Patel: On costs, we ran a quick calc: during the spike our effective per-invocation cost ~2.3x baseline. We need guidance on how to avoid that.
[01:58] Maya Chen: Totally. Two levers — smarter autoscaler config + short-term routing to lower-cost model variants during bursts. Also prefix caching tuning and a burst pool on Dedicated can mitigate.
[02:08] Anita Shah: Can you quantify the Dedicated benefit vs hosted? We're worried about committing to monthly capacity without seeing the numbers for our burst profile.
[02:17] Luis Ortega: We'll run a dedicated pilot benchmark using your 512-token 95th percentile profile, include warm KV cache and cold-start sims. That will give a per-token and per-peak-hour cost delta.
[02:26] Jordan Blake: Awesome. Timeline?
[02:29] Luis Ortega: If we get histograms by end of Thursday (you mentioned 3/19), I can have a solid run and initial spreadsheet by the 23rd.
[02:36] Maya Chen: We'll include a model mix suggestion — e.g., serve gpt-like open model for low-latency paths and fall back to a cheaper quantized variant for long context batch jobs.
[02:45] Ellen Cho: For security, our CISO wants to confirm KMS/HSM integration and audit log retention. Are those in the security pack?
[02:52] Priya Nair: Yes, Priya here — we'll send the security pack with SOC2 cert, details on KMS integrations (AWS KMS / customer HSM options) and sample audit logs. We'll also outline SSO / SAML steps.
[03:03] Samir Patel: Great. Also need to know data residency options — our EU traffic must stay in eu-west-1 region.
[03:09] Maya Chen: Region pinning is supported in Dedicated and in our Private offering. We can show the routing policy that pins model inference to eu-west-1.
[03:16] Jordan Blake: There's also the question of failure modes — what happens if dedicated pool is saturated? Do requests fallback to hosted? Is that automatic?
[03:24] Luis Ortega: We can implement a policy to fallback to a compatible hosted variant or a smaller model. It can be automatic with circuit-breaker style rules. We can demo that in the pilot.
[03:33] Anita Shah: From an engineering ops side, we need tracing hooks into our observability stack, ideally distributed tracing correlation IDs so our SREs can tie traces to our traces.
[03:44] Maya Chen: Absolutely — we expose trace headers and have an open telemetry integration example. We'll share the example snippet.
[03:51] Jordan Blake: On the pilot shape — we expect a 4 week pilot: 1 week integration, 2 weeks benchmark (warm + cold scenarios), 1 week burn-in and SLA run. Is that what you're recommending?
[04:03] Luis Ortega: That aligns to what I'd recommend. We'll put together a runbook showing the exact tests — p95/p99 latency, cost per token, cold start profile, KV cache hit rate.
[04:13] Samir Patel: One concern — the billing model. How granular are the dedicated invoices? We want per-hour and per-token reporting to match our chargeback.
[04:21] Priya Nair: Dedicated invoices include hourly capacity charges and per-token consumption for burst usage above commit. We can provide token-level CSVs for your internal chargeback.
[04:29] Anita Shah: Great. Also we want role-based access control for the console — can we map to our AD groups?
[04:36] Maya Chen: Yes SSO + SCIM provisioning is supported, you can map roles to AD groups. We'll include mapping docs.
[04:42] Jordan Blake: Any blockers on our side? We need to get you the traffic histograms and sample API keys for the benchmark.
[04:50] Ellen Cho: For security we will not share real keys, we'll provide equivalent test keys and a sanitized sample. Also share the contact for our infra team.
[04:58] Luis Ortega: Perfect. For the benchmark, best if you give us a 7-day rolling histogram and an example of your 95th percentile request size distribution.
[05:06] Maya Chen: I'll send a packet with pricing, the pilot contract template, and the security pack. Expect that by Thursday morning.
[05:12] Jordan Blake: Good. A couple of nitty-gritty questions from our SRE — are there rate limit guards to protect downstream stateful services?
[05:20] Luis Ortega: Yes, request shaping and token rate limiting can be applied per-route. Also you can set circuit-breaker thresholds so when the model pool degrades it fails fast instead of backpressuring your DBs.
[05:32] Anita Shah: On the reliability incidents — you mentioned autoscaler config — is that something you can help tune during the pilot? We don't want repeated bounces.
[05:39] Luis Ortega: We'll co-tune the autoscaler policy. Two knobs typically: scaling cooldown and cross-request batching window. Tuning them reduces churn and improves batching.
[05:48] Samir Patel: What's the expected unit cost change if we go to a 2:1 reserved commit vs current on-demand? Rough ballpark.
[05:56] Maya Chen: Ballpark depends a lot on model family and GPU type, but usually committed capacity can reduce base hourly unit cost 30–45% depending on commit length and GPU class. The spreadsheet will show your specific numbers.
[06:08] Jordan Blake: Okay, I'm going to hand over to Ellen for ops questions.
[06:12] Ellen Cho: Thanks. When you talked about audit logs retention, what's the default retention window and are longer windows available?
[06:18] Priya Nair: Default is 90 days for the hosted plan. Longer retention (1 year+) is available as an add-on for Dedicated/Private. We can include retention pricing.
[06:27] Ellen Cho: Good. Also, for the vault integration — do we support customer-managed keys in GCP and AWS?
[06:33] Maya Chen: Yes both. Customer-managed keys are supported for storage encryption and model payload encryption. We'll document the KMS flows.
[06:40] Anita Shah: A small tangent: we noticed some model output variance after a recent model swap. Could that be because of quantization differences?
[06:47] Luis Ortega: Possibly. If different model variants use different quantization/compilers, you can see slight output drift. We suggest running a small eval suite before switching. Redwood Optimize can give recommendations.
[06:59] Jordan Blake: Is Redwood Optimize included in pilot?
[07:02] Maya Chen: Not included by default, but we can enable a limited Optimize trial for the POC so you get quantization and batching suggestions.
[07:09] Samir Patel: For the pilot rollout policy — we want canary with auto rollback on quality regression. Is there an automated A/B tool?
[07:16] Luis Ortega: Yes, our rollout supports canary and A/B with metric gating; you can set quality thresholds tied to eval sets and auto rollback if thresholds fail. We'll show a demo.
[07:25] Anita Shah: Demo scheduling request — can we do a targeted technical deep dive for SRE and infra next Wed? 60 minutes.
[07:31] Maya Chen: I'll coordinate. Luis, can you lead?
[07:34] Luis Ortega: Yep, I can.
[07:36] Jordan Blake: On contractual terms — we need an SLA with uptime and latency targets for dedicated pools. Can we get a draft?
[07:42] Maya Chen: We'll share a standard SLA and can negotiate enterprise terms in the pilot contract.
[07:47] Samir Patel: Anything else on costs? Any hidden fees we should know about?
[07:51] Priya Nair: No hidden fees — main components are capacity commit, per-token consumption for burst overage, premium support if chosen, and add-ons like extended audit retention. We'll provide a sample invoice layout.
[08:02] Jordan Blake: Cool. Let's recap next steps.
[08:05] Maya Chen: Recap: 1) Pelican provides histograms + sample request shapes by 2026-03-19. 2) We send security pack + pricing + pilot contract by 2026-03-19. 3) Luis schedules benchmark and runs by 2026-03-23. 4) Deep technical SRE dive scheduled for next Wed (Maya/Luis lead).
[08:28] Jordan Blake: Sounds good. Anything else?
[08:31] Anita Shah: Just one more, can you include an example of token-level CSVs for chargeback?
[08:35] Priya Nair: Yes will include.
[08:37] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll get those artifacts out.
[08:40] Samir Patel: Thanks all.
[08:42] End of recording.

Notes about transcript quality: speaker turns sometimes overlap, product names occasionally misspelled (e.g., "K V cash"), timestamps approximate. Shared artifacts referenced: https://drive.redwood/pelican/pilot-plan (pilot runbook), https://drive.redwood/pelican/security-pack (security pack + SOC2).

Final recap (from meeting):
- Business need: reduce cost volatility and keep p99 latency < 180ms for interactive flows
- Proposed pilot: 4-week dedicated pilot with warm/cold benchmarks and SLA burn-in
- Deliverables from Redwood: cost model, pilot runbook, security pack, benchmark results and recommended autoscaler & cache configs
- Deliverables from Pelican: traffic histograms, sample sanitized keys, infra contact, confirmation of target SLA
